sentences.text:
Kosaraju Srinivasa Rao, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 23
October, 2019

Author: T. Rajani
Bench: T. Rajani
 Smt. Justice T.Rajani
 Criminal Petition No. 6333 Of 2019
Order:

This criminal petition is filed, under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short,
'Cr.P.C.'), by the petitioners-accused Nos. 1 and 2 seeking for quash of the proceedings against them in C.C.No. 381 of 2018 on the file of the Court of I Additional Junior Civil Judge, Tenali (for short,
'the Court below'), registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 272, 273 and 188 IPC and Sections 57, 58 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the Act').
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that this case is squarely covered by order of High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh in Criminal Petition Nos. 3731 of 2018 and batch dated 27-08-2018, wherein the Court, by considering that tobacco products would not fall within the purview of IPC and that therefore the police are not authorized to register crime, investigate and file charge sheet, quashed the proceedings against the petitioners therein.
4.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: With regard to Section 188 IPC also, it is observed that as per Section 195 (1) (a) (i) of Cr.P.C., no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the compliant in writing of that Court or by such officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
In this case, FIR is registered suo motu basing on the report of Sub Inspector of Police.
Hence, there is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C. so far as Section 188 IPC is concerned.

5. With regard to the offences under Sections 57, 58 and 63 of the Act, in Criminal Petition Nos. 3731 of 2018 and batch, the Court quashed the proceedings by considering the case of Messrs.
Vaipugaiyilai Urpathiyalargal Matrum Virpanaiyalargal Nala Sangam Vs. The Commissioner of Food Safety1, wherein an identical question, whether chewing tobacco manufacturers come within the purview of the Act and Food Safety Officer is competent to investigate and to file charge sheet,
came up for consideration and it was held that chewing tobacco is covered by Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce,
Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 and Food Safety Officer is not an authority to Kosaraju Srinivasa Rao, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 23 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123511882/
1 interfere with the business of the petitioner.

sentences.text: 6. Hence, in the light of the above judgments, this Court opines that the proceedings against the petitioners, who also stand on the same footing, in C.C.No. 381 of 2018 on the file of the Court below have to be quashed and the same are accordingly quashed.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed in consequence.

T. RAJANI, J.
JSK W.P. (MD) No. 10319 OF 2017 SMT.
